items.title: Teacher noticing in K–12 science education: a literature review of its role in students’ scientific thinking

ai.headline: Teachers who notice students’ science thinking can help create better conditions for scientific reasoning.
ai.summary: This literature review looked at 17 studies on how K–12 science teachers attend to, interpret, and respond to students’ thinking. Teachers noticed everyday language, questions, drawings, and inquiry practices, and interpreted their scientific meaning, but direct evidence linking noticing to long-term student development is limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how classroom interactions can support or limit how young people learn to think scientifically.
ai.life_skill: Notice how someone explains an idea before jumping in to correct them.
ai.fact: Scientific thinking includes inquiry, systematic observation, evidence evaluation, explanation construction, conceptual revision, and collaborative knowledge building.

quiz.question: What did the review find about teachers’ responses to student thinking?
quiz.answer: Teachers often attended to and interpreted student thinking, but enacted instructional responses were studied less often.

ai.caveat: It is an integrative narrative review of 17 empirical studies, so it identifies patterns rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: Why do people prefer human empathy despite rating AI empathy higher?

ai.headline: People may prefer human empathy even when they rate AI empathy as higher.
ai.summary: The piece asks whether AI-generated empathy can replace human connection as more people use chatbots for companionship and loneliness. It notes that people can rate AI empathy highly yet still prefer human empathy.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights a gap between rating empathy and actually wanting it from a person rather than a machine.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you prefer talking to a person or a chatbot when you feel lonely.
ai.fact: More people are turning to AI-powered chatbots for companionship and to address loneliness.

quiz.question: What does the article question about AI-generated empathy?
quiz.answer: Whether it can replace human connection.

items.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities

ai.headline: A new AI model can parse text, images, audio and video into structured records using one shared system.
ai.summary: The paper introduces Youtu-Parsing-Omni, an omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio and video into structured records grounded in space and time. Using one encoder for all modalities and one schema for all tasks, it achieves top results on several parsing benchmarks, especially for audio and video.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a single AI system might one day help people search, cite and organise information across different media types.
ai.life_skill: Try checking whether an AI tool can handle audio and video as well as text before relying on it for research.
ai.fact: Youtu-Parsing-Omni scored 96.96 overall on OmniDocBench v1.6 and 75.08 average on OmniParsingBench, leading open-weight models.

quiz.question: What does Youtu-Parsing-Omni convert documents, images, audio and video into?
quiz.answer: Structured records grounded in space and time.

items.title: Evaluation of the Asthma Management Program to Promote Activity for Students in Schools (Asthma-PASS)

ai.summary: The study evaluates a multifaceted school-based intervention designed to address barriers to physical activity among urban schoolchildren with asthma, with the goal of reducing asthma morbidity.

items.title: A simple blood test could reveal Alzheimer’s risk 10 years before symptoms

ai.summary: A major international study examined whether a simple blood test could predict Alzheimer’s-related cognitive decline before symptoms appear. Researchers say this could lead to earlier intervention and future preventive treatments.

ai.fact: A blood test may be able to predict Alzheimer’s-related cognitive decline years before symptoms appear.

items.title: Rare damselfly spotted by restored chalk river

ai.summary: A news report says a rare damselfly was spotted by a restored chalk river. The Herts and Middlesex Trust says its new wetlands are helping species thrive. The report gives no study details, numbers, or scientific evidence.

items.title: Molecular and functional analysis of calcium binding by a cancer-linked calreticulin mutant

ai.headline: A cancer-linked calreticulin mutant still binds calcium, and cells compensate when the protein is missing.
ai.summary: Scientists studied a mutated form of calreticulin, a protein linked to some blood cancers, to test whether it still binds calcium. They found the mutant keeps similar low-affinity calcium-binding ability to the normal protein, and cells lacking calreticulin adjust other proteins to keep calcium levels steady.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how cells may compensate for faulty proteins, which is relevant to understanding how certain blood cancers develop.
ai.fact: Cells can make up for missing calreticulin by changing other proteins that control calcium inside the endoplasmic reticulum.

quiz.question: Does the cancer-linked calreticulin mutant Del52 completely lose its ability to bind calcium?
quiz.answer: No, it retains similar low-affinity calcium-binding characteristics to the normal protein.

ai.caveat: The results come from lab experiments with proteins and engineered cells, so they do not show what happens in people living with blood cancer.

items.title: Optimal Taxation of Indistinguishable Activities -- by Jacob Goldin, Sebastian Koehne, Nicholas Lawson

ai.headline: When tax rules can't separate business from personal spending, one deduction rate must balance both behaviours.
ai.summary: The study looks at how governments should set a single tax deduction for expenses that are hard to tell apart, such as business versus personal air travel. It finds the best rate depends on how people's spending changes on each side, weighted by the tax wedge, and measures the benefit of being able to distinguish the two.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why tax systems often use blunt rules for expenses and what policymakers give up when they cannot separate work and personal costs.
ai.fact: A single tax deduction rate for mixed business and personal spending is optimal when it balances how people respond to taxes on each type of spending.

quiz.question: What does the paper say determines the best single tax deduction rate for hard-to-distinguish expenses?
quiz.answer: It turns on the relative compensated spending response for each type of spending, weighted by the income tax wedge.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and is based on a theoretical model rather than real-world evidence.

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden driver of high cholesterol and a way to stop it

ai.headline: Blocking a hidden mechanism lowered LDL cholesterol in mice, and an early human drug safety trial passed.
ai.summary: Researchers studied how high-cholesterol diets can weaken the body's natural cholesterol defences. In mice, blocking this hidden mechanism dramatically lowered harmful LDL cholesterol. An experimental drug targeting the same pathway has passed an early human safety trial.

ai.fact: High-cholesterol diets can undermine the body's natural cholesterol defences in mice.

quiz.question: What did blocking the hidden mechanism do to harmful LDL cholesterol in mice?
quiz.answer: It dramatically lowered it.

ai.summary: Researchers studied global preferences for caesarean delivery among pregnant women. They found that 26% of women preferred caesarean delivery and identified factors associated with this preference. These factors included age, education, and prior pregnancy complications.

ai.headline: Postnatal care uptake is inconsistent
ai.summary: Researchers studied postnatal care provision and uptake in sub-Saharan Africa. They found that despite high service availability, uptake was only 42%. Providers and women identified several barriers to utilisation, including inadequate staffing and limited knowledge.

items.title: Knowledge, attitude, and practices towards anthrax among Communities in the Southern and South-western Ethiopia

ai.headline: In rural Ethiopia, many people know about anthrax but still handle dead animals unsafely.
ai.summary: This cross-sectional study interviewed 382 household heads in southern and southwestern Ethiopia about their knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding anthrax. items.title: Enablers and barriers to scaling an ECD parenting program into primary health care services in rural Bangladesh

items.title: The generative paradox: the Anti-Prompt paradigm for human capability

ai.headline: AI should help people keep their own skills, not just produce better results together.
ai.summary: The paper argues that judging AI only by joint human-AI output misses whether people can still understand, challenge, repair and adapt work when AI support changes or disappears. It calls this tension the generative paradox and proposes an Anti-Prompt approach where AI first creates conditions for human construction instead of generating immediately.
ai.why_it_matters: It matters because relying on AI for answers can quietly erode the very skills people need to work independently later.
ai.life_skill: Try solving a problem yourself before asking AI for help, so you keep your own understanding and ability to adapt.
ai.fact: Judging AI only by joint human-AI output can overlook whether people retain the ability to understand, challenge, repair and adapt work when support changes or disappears.

quiz.question: What does the Anti-Prompt paradigm do differently?
quiz.answer: It reverses the usual order so AI first creates conditions for human construction instead of generating immediately.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and presents a conceptual proposal rather than tested evidence.

items.title: Salience network expansion as a transdiagnostic neural marker for psychopathology risk in adolescence

items.title: Making argumentative work visible in GenAI-mediated assessment: an exploratory LLM simulation and questionnaire study in university ideological and political education

items.title: Pregnant women’s health beliefs about pre-eclampsia in a resource-limited setting: A qualitative study

ai.headline: Pregnant women in Ghana see pre-eclampsia as serious but face cost, mistrust and poor communication when seeking care.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 16 pregnant women in Ghana’s Ashanti Region about their beliefs regarding pre-eclampsia. Women viewed the condition as serious and recognised antenatal care and lifestyle changes as beneficial, yet barriers such as financial constraints, mistrust of the health system and inadequate provider communication hindered care-seeking.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding women’s beliefs and barriers can help health services communicate risks more clearly and encourage earlier care for a dangerous pregnancy complication.
ai.life_skill: Notice and ask about warning signs in pregnancy, and discuss any concerns with a qualified health professional early.
ai.fact: Pre-eclampsia is a high-risk pregnancy complication that threatens maternal and fetal health.

quiz.question: What did the women in the study identify as barriers to seeking care for pre-eclampsia?
quiz.answer: Financial constraints, mistrust of the health system, and inadequate communication from health providers.

ai.caveat: This small qualitative study in one Ghanaian district hospital cannot prove effects or generalise to other settings.

items.title: Empirical validation of a predicted emotional modulation dimension linking temporal variability and individual differences in PTSD

ai.headline: PTSD symptoms fluctuate along a specific balance between re-experiencing and avoidance, not just overall severity.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed data from nine PTSD cohorts to see if symptom changes over time follow the same patterns as differences between people. They found that both individual differences and daily fluctuations are organised by a 'symptom imbalance' axis, where two common therapies reduce severity but shift this balance in opposite directions.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that how a person's symptoms shift day-to-day might be as important as their overall severity for understanding recovery and choosing the right support.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your stress response tends to involve replaying events or avoiding triggers, as this pattern may differ from others.
ai.fact: Cognitive processing therapy and EMDR reduce overall PTSD severity but move symptoms in opposite directions along the re-experiencing-avoidance balance.

quiz.question: Did the two therapies studied produce the same change in symptom imbalance?
quiz.answer: No, they produced opposite shifts along the symptom imbalance axis while both reduced overall severity.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it uses statistical modelling of existing data rather than a randomised trial to prove causation.

items.title: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation

ai.headline: A new framework checks whether AI computer-use agents notice changes that happen while they work.
ai.summary: The paper introduces EnvOS, a way to test AI agents in software that changes mid-task, such as an appointment moving or a policy being revised. In clinic booking, Claude Opus 5 succeeded on 0 out of 16 tasks when nothing extra was shown, 2 out of 16 when reminded to re-check, and 15 out of 16 when the updated value was shown. The framework also caught most corrupted or wrongly graded episodes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI helpers can miss updates in the apps they use, so people should not assume an agent has seen the latest information.
ai.life_skill: Check that an AI agent has re-read the latest screen before acting on information it found earlier.
ai.fact: EnvOS tests whether AI agents notice mid-task changes and verifies that graders score them correctly.

quiz.question: In clinic booking, how many of 16 tasks did Claude Opus 5 succeed at when the updated value was shown?
quiz.answer: It succeeded on 15 out of 16 tasks.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the results come from a small set of tasks with two AI models.

items.title: Experimental evolution unveils a role for structural variants and sex-specificity in the genetic architecture of lifespan

ai.headline: Lifespan in beetles is shaped by many genes, including structural DNA changes, with some differences between sexes.
ai.summary: Researchers bred seed beetles for over 200 generations to create short- and long-lived lines, nearly doubling lifespan. Whole-genome sequencing found more than 700 genes under selection, over 600 genes in copy-number variant regions, and many small-effect genetic regions, with four regions showing strong sex-specific effects.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that lifespan is influenced by many genetic factors working together and can differ between males and females, helping scientists understand the biology of ageing.
ai.fact: Lifespan evolution in beetles involved many genes and structural DNA changes, with some effects differing between the sexes.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find about genetic effects on lifespan between males and females?
quiz.answer: Genetic effects were mostly similar between the sexes, but four regions showed pronounced sex differences.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and was done in seed beetles, so the findings may not apply to humans.

items.title: Process visualization feedback in news translation: a controlled intervention study of human-AI interaction using multimodal process data

ai.headline: Seeing a visual map of your work process helps you spot deeper mistakes and use tools more strategically.
ai.summary: This study gave translation students a visual record of their work process to review, rather than just feedback on the final result. Those who saw this 'process visualization' made more meaningful changes to their text and used search tools more effectively than those who only received standard feedback.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that understanding *how* you work, not just *what* you produce, can help you improve your skills and become more independent in your learning.
ai.life_skill: When reviewing your own work, try to look at your process (like how long you spent on each part) to spot where you get stuck.
ai.fact: Reviewing a visual record of your work process is linked to a shift from fixing surface errors to making deeper, substantive improvements.

quiz.question: What did the students in the experimental group receive that the control group did not?
quiz.answer: The experimental group received personalized process visualizations and structured reflection, while the control group received conventional product-oriented feedback.

ai.caveat: The study involved a small group of 22 translation students, so it is unclear if these results apply to other types of work or general learners.

items.title: Calling species 'invasive'—and culling them—isn't done lightly. But it matters to Australia's threatened species

ai.headline: Calling a species invasive can determine whether it is culled or left alone in Australia.
ai.summary: The piece explains that labels such as native, introduced or invasive matter because they shape whether animals are culled. In Australia, species like European rabbits and feral pigs are often culled, while most native animals are generally left alone.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how language about nature can directly affect which animals live or die.
ai.life_skill: Check how a species is classified before assuming whether it is protected or considered a pest.
ai.fact: Species considered invasive in Australia, such as European rabbits and feral pigs, are often culled.

quiz.question: What can happen to species considered invasive in Australia?
quiz.answer: They are often culled, while most native animals are generally left alone.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed study, so it does not provide direct evidence of effects or outcomes.

items.title: Neutrophil RAGE drives early cerebrovascular injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage

ai.headline: A protein on immune cells called RAGE may drive early brain blood vessel damage after a bleed on the brain.
ai.summary: Researchers from Japan and the United States studied subarachnoid hemorrhage, a type of bleeding around the brain. They found that neutrophil RAGE, a receptor on immune cells, plays a key role in causing early injury to brain blood vessels after this event.
ai.why_it_matters: It points to a possible biological mechanism behind brain damage after a serious bleed, which could help scientists understand how such injuries develop.
ai.fact: Neutrophil RAGE is linked to early cerebrovascular injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage.

quiz.question: What did researchers identify as a key driver of early cerebrovascular injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage?
quiz.answer: Neutrophil RAGE, a receptor on immune cells.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about early-stage research, not proof that targeting RAGE will help people.

items.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training

ai.headline: Matching effective learning rate trajectories makes weight-normalized and weight-decay training behave similarly.
ai.summary: The study compared weight-normalized training with conventional weight decay and found that performance gains come mainly from the effective learning rate trajectory, not normalization alone. A new schedule called AIR outperformed cosine and other schedules in large-scale pretraining experiments.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how a learning rate changes over time matters more than the starting rate, which is useful for anyone training machine-learning models.
ai.life_skill: Try focusing on how a setting changes over time rather than just its starting value when learning a new skill.
ai.fact: Matching effective learning rate trajectories collapses the training loss dynamics of weight-normalized and weight-decay training.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find drives the gains in weight-normalized training?
quiz.answer: The gains are driven primarily by the induced effective learning rate trajectory rather than normalization alone.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the experiments focus on large-scale pretraining rather than everyday learning.

items.title: Cannabidiol and Prolonged Exposure

ai.headline: A trial will test whether CBD can improve prolonged exposure therapy for veterans with PTSD.
ai.summary: A randomised controlled trial plans to compare prolonged exposure therapy plus cannabidiol (CBD) with prolonged exposure therapy plus placebo in 136 military veterans with PTSD at the VA San Diego Medical Center. Results are not yet reported; the study aims to see if adding CBD improves treatment outcomes.
ai.why_it_matters: It could help shape future care for veterans living with PTSD if CBD proves useful as an add-on to therapy.

quiz.question: What will the trial compare in veterans with PTSD?
quiz.answer: It will compare prolonged exposure therapy plus CBD with prolonged exposure therapy plus placebo.

ai.caveat: This is a planned trial posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, not a completed study with results, so no conclusions can yet be drawn.

items.title: Scientists say a forgotten particle may explain why the universe exists

ai.headline: Scientists propose an overlooked neutrino may explain why matter survived the Big Bang.
ai.summary: The paper discusses a mysterious particle overlooked for decades that may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang. Scientists believe this forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have left detectable gravitational wave signals.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps us understand how the universe came to exist and how stars, planets, and life became possible.
ai.fact: A forgotten neutrino may explain why matter survived the Big Bang.

quiz.question: What particle may explain why matter survived the Big Bang?
quiz.answer: A forgotten neutrino may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a scientific proposal, not peer-reviewed proof.

items.title: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years

ai.headline: A rare beetle thought extinct in Wales has been found again after 60 years.
ai.summary: Surveys had raised fears that the Short-Necked Oil Beetle had disappeared from Wales. The beetle has now been found again in Wales after six decades.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that species thought lost can still survive, highlighting the value of checking and protecting natural habitats.
ai.life_skill: Notice and report unusual insects you see to local wildlife groups.
ai.fact: The Short-Necked Oil Beetle was found in Wales again after 60 years.

quiz.question: What happened to the Short-Necked Oil Beetle in Wales after 60 years?
quiz.answer: It was found again after surveys had feared it had become extinct.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed scientific study, so details are limited.

items.title: Assessment of psychological problems in children with chronic physical health conditions using DSM-oriented ASEBA scales: a meta-analysis.

ai.headline: Children with long-term physical health conditions show higher scores on all mental-health problem scales, especially somatic and affective problems.
ai.summary: This meta-analysis combined 115 studies comparing DSM-oriented ASEBA scores in 12,958 children and adolescents with chronic physical health conditions against 24,638 controls. Elevated scores were found on every scale, with the largest differences for somatic and affective problems, and between 8.6% and 14.3% scored in the clinical range depending on the scale.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that young people managing long-term physical illness often also face emotional and physical-symptom distress, so routine mental-health screening can matter alongside physical care.
ai.life_skill: Notice if a young person with a long-term health condition seems persistently low, worried, or focused on physical symptoms, and encourage them or their family to speak with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Children and adolescents with chronic physical health conditions are more likely to score in the clinical range on affective problems than on attention-deficit/hyperactivity problems.

quiz.question: Which two DSM-oriented scales showed the largest differences between young people with chronic physical health conditions and controls?
quiz.answer: Somatic Problems and Affective Problems showed the highest effect sizes.

ai.caveat: The included studies were mostly observational comparisons rather than randomised trials, so the findings show associations rather than proving that the physical condition caused the higher scores.

items.title: The impact of martial arts-based interventions on cognitive function and motor performance in elementary school-aged children: a systematic review
items.venue: Pedagogy of Physical Culture and Sports

ai.headline: Martial arts may help children’s attention, self-control, balance and fitness, but are not proven better than other exercise.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 12 studies with about 1,300 children aged 6–12 found that martial arts programmes such as taekwondo and karate were linked to improvements in attention, self-regulation, balance, coordination and cardiorespiratory fitness. The evidence was mixed in quality and did not show martial arts are superior to other well-designed physical activity programmes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that structured movement with rules and self-control can support skills useful in school and daily life, though more research is needed.
ai.life_skill: Try a structured activity that combines movement, balance and clear rules, such as a beginner martial arts class, and notice whether it helps your focus.
ai.fact: Martial arts-based interventions were linked to improvements in attention, self-regulation, balance, coordination and cardiorespiratory fitness in children aged 6–12.

quiz.question: What did the review find about martial arts compared with other physical activity programmes?
quiz.answer: It found possible benefits but did not establish that martial arts are superior to other well-designed physical activity programmes.

ai.caveat: The studies varied in methods and several had concerns or serious risk of bias, so the findings are not definitive proof.

items.title: Effects of Parent-Involved Digital Health Interventions on Adiposity-Related Outcomes and Behaviors in Children and Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

ai.headline: Digital health programmes involving parents may slightly lower BMI in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at 29 randomised trials involving 4,156 children and adolescents with overweight or obesity. Parent-involved digital health interventions produced a small but statistically significant reduction in BMI-related outcomes compared with controls, though effects on diet, physical activity and sedentary behaviour were limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that involving parents through digital tools can support modest weight-related improvements in young people, but it is not a complete solution on its own.
ai.life_skill: Try involving a parent or caregiver when using a digital health app or programme to support healthier eating and activity habits.
ai.fact: Parent-involved digital health interventions were linked to a small reduction in BMI-related outcomes in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity.

quiz.question: What did parent-involved digital health interventions do to BMI-related outcomes compared with controls?
quiz.answer: They produced a small but statistically significant reduction in BMI-related outcomes.

ai.caveat: The evidence is moderate certainty, and the best digital delivery method or parent-involved strategy has not yet been established.

items.title: Systematic Review of the Association Between Sleep and Depression Among Korean Adolescents
items.venue: Asia-pacific Journal of Convergent Research Interchange

ai.headline: Poor sleep is linked to higher depressive symptoms in Korean adolescents.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at nine studies of Korean middle and high school students. It found that short sleep duration, poor sleep quality, insufficient sleep, insomnia, daytime sleepiness, later bedtime and evening chronotype were consistently linked to increased depressive symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: Sleep habits may be an important part of adolescent mental health, though the review cannot show whether poor sleep causes depression.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your sleep patterns relate to your mood and consider speaking with a trusted adult or health professional if sleep problems persist.
ai.fact: Short sleep duration, poor sleep quality, insufficient sleep, insomnia, excessive daytime sleepiness, later bedtime and evening chronotype were consistently associated with increased depressive symptoms among Korean adolescents.

quiz.question: What did all nine studies in the review report about sleep-related factors and depression?
quiz.answer: All nine studies reported that at least one sleep-related factor was significantly associated with depression or depressive symptoms.

ai.caveat: The included studies were observational, so they show links rather than prove that sleep problems cause depression, and further longitudinal research is needed.

items.title: Living evidence map of the global climate and health literature.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Researchers are building a living map of global studies linking climate change and human health.
ai.summary: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review that plans to systematically map the worldwide literature on how climate change, weather, climate-forcing agents and fossil fuels relate to human health and well-being. It will be updated continuously and made searchable through an interactive interface.
ai.why_it_matters: It will help people see what research exists on climate-related health risks and where evidence is missing.
ai.life_skill: Check a trusted evidence map or health organisation for up-to-date information on climate-related health risks in your area.
ai.fact: Climate change, climate variability, weather, climate-forcing agents and fossil fuels are being studied for their links to human health and well-being.

quiz.question: What is the main aim of this Cochrane review?
quiz.answer: To systematically map the global literature on the relationship between climate-related factors and human health and well-being.

ai.caveat: This is only a protocol describing what the review plans to do, not a completed review with findings.

items.title: Infectious disease outbreaks among hospitalised neonates in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Drug-resistant Klebsiella bacteria cause most neonatal outbreaks in LMIC hospitals.
ai.summary: The review looked at 172 outbreaks in newborn units across 32 low- and middle-income countries. Gram-negative bacteria caused 74% of outbreaks, with Klebsiella spp. most common and often resistant to key antibiotics.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how antibiotic-resistant infections can spread in hospitals where newborns are cared for, highlighting why infection prevention matters worldwide.
ai.life_skill: Notice and ask about hand hygiene and cleaning practices when visiting healthcare settings.
ai.fact: Klebsiella spp. was the most frequently detected outbreak pathogen in neonatal units in LMICs.

quiz.question: What proportion of outbreaks were caused by Gram-negative bacteria?
quiz.answer: Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 74% of outbreaks.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and reporting deficiencies plus potential publication bias limited some analyses.

items.title: Models of Supportive Care for Parents of Infants in Neonatal Intensive Care Units: A Systematic Review of Their Characteristics and Outcome

ai.headline: Different supportive care models may help lower stress for parents of premature babies in neonatal intensive care.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 17 studies of supportive care models for parents with premature infants in NICUs. It identified six models, including family-centred care, kangaroo mother care, peer support and specialised father support, and found they are linked to reduced parental stress, greater parental engagement and efficacy, and better health outcomes for parents.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that structured support for parents during a baby’s NICU stay can matter for family wellbeing, which is useful for anyone wanting to understand how hospitals might help families cope.
ai.life_skill: Notice what support services are available for parents in a neonatal unit and consider using them if you or someone you know is affected.
ai.fact: Six supportive care models for parents of premature infants in NICUs were identified in the review.

quiz.question: How many supportive care models for parents of premature infants in NICUs did the review identify?
quiz.answer: The review identified six possible supportive care models.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and most of the included studies were rated only moderate quality.

items.title: Effectiveness of Stepped Care Psychological Interventions in Children and Adolescents: A Meta-Analytic Review

ai.headline: Stepped care mental health support for young people works about as well as usual care but costs less.
ai.summary: This preprint reviewed studies of stepped care, where children and adolescents start with lighter support and move to more intensive help only if needed. It found similar mental health outcomes to standard care, including intensive treatments, but significantly lower costs.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how mental health services might help more young people without spending more money.
ai.life_skill: Notice if your mental health support feels too intense or too light, and ask a trusted adult or professional about other options.
ai.fact: About 46% of young people in the reviewed studies moved from the first step of care to a later step.

quiz.question: Did stepped care produce better mental health results than control conditions?
quiz.answer: No, effects compared with control conditions were small and non-significant, meaning outcomes were comparable rather than superior.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not final proof.

items.title: Effect of nutrition counseling on complementary feeding practices among mothers with children aged 6–23 months in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia: A cluster-randomized controlled trial

ai.headline: Nutrition counseling helped Ethiopian mothers feed young children more appropriately.
ai.summary: A cluster-randomised trial in rural Northwest Ethiopia compared mothers who received monthly Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling with mothers who received routine education. Counselled mothers were nearly 2.5 times more likely to practice appropriate complementary feeding, and their children were more likely to meet dietary diversity, meal frequency, and acceptable diet targets.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that structured counseling can improve how young children are fed in similar rural communities, supporting child growth and development.
ai.life_skill: Try asking a qualified health worker or nutritionist for practical advice on what and how often to feed a child aged 6–23 months.
ai.fact: Appropriate complementary feeding is essential for children’s growth and cognitive development.

quiz.question: What did the study find about mothers who received nutrition counseling compared with those who received routine education?
quiz.answer: They were nearly 2.5 times more likely to practice appropriate complementary feeding.

ai.caveat: The results come from one trial in rural Northwest Ethiopia, so they may not apply to other settings.

items.title: Advance Care Planning Impact on the Consistency of Older Adults With Lung Cancer and Their Potential Surrogates Regarding Life-Sustaining Treatment Preferences

ai.headline: A tabletop game helped older adults with lung cancer and their chosen surrogates agree more on life-sustaining treatment choices than a standard manual.
ai.summary: This randomised trial compared an advance care planning tabletop game called “Walking with Wishes” with a standard advance care planning manual in patient–surrogate pairs. The game reduced the gap between patients’ and surrogates’ preferences for five life-sustaining treatments across nine health scenarios, and did not increase state anxiety for either group.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a simple, low-cost activity can help families understand each other’s wishes about serious medical treatment before a crisis happens.
ai.life_skill: Try talking with a trusted friend or relative about what medical treatments you would or would not want if you became seriously ill.
ai.fact: Advance care planning is the process of discussing and recording preferences for future medical care.
ai.caveat: This is a single trial posted as results on a clinical trials register, so the findings should be treated as preliminary until fully published and peer reviewed.

items.title: The Price of a Chance in Artificial Societies

ai.headline: Reward design changes how simulated agents compete and how much they spend chasing prizes.
ai.summary: Researchers simulated 200 LLM agents competing over 50 rounds to maximise wealth. At low rewards agents invested little, while at high rewards they overcompeted, especially when prize coverage was intermediate. Smaller prizes spread across more winners reduced investment while keeping selection quality similar, but broader coverage lowered selection quality.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how prize structures can shape competition and the costs people bear chasing uncertain rewards.
ai.life_skill: Notice how the size and spread of a prize affects how much effort you are willing to put in.
ai.fact: Agents near the qualification cutoff can invest heavily yet receive no prize and finish poorer than non-winners who invest less.

quiz.question: What happened when smaller prizes were offered to more winners?
quiz.answer: Investment reduced while selection quality was preserved relative to the corresponding top-ability target.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint simulation of artificial LLM agents, not peer-reviewed evidence about real people.

items.title: Sex differences in latent inhibition and their implications for psychotic disorders

ai.headline: Research suggests sex differences in latent inhibition may be linked to psychosis risk, but evidence is mixed.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined studies of latent inhibition in humans and rodents. It found mostly inconclusive evidence for sex differences, though differences were more likely when factors such as drug treatment, juvenile handling, or oestrous phase were involved. New rodent data also suggest sex differences in hippocampal processing during latent inhibition.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how biological sex might influence learning processes linked to hallucinations and delusions in psychosis.
ai.life_skill: Notice how prior exposure to a harmless cue can reduce your attention to it later, and consider whether stress or other factors change that effect for you.
ai.fact: Latent inhibition is the reduced ability to learn about a stimulus after prior exposure to it without consequence.

quiz.question: What did the systematic review find about sex differences in latent inhibition?
quiz.answer: Evidence was predominantly inconclusive and conflicting, with stronger indications of sex differences when additional factors such as drug administration, juvenile handling, or oestrous phase were studied.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the underlying evidence is described as mostly inconclusive and conflicting.

items.title: Socio-occupational factors and problematic internet use: indirect associations involving negative affect and impulsivity in a predominantly urban, highly educated Romanian adult sample

ai.headline: Lower social support and work engagement, plus higher work addiction, link to problematic internet use via negative mood and impulsivity.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 215 mostly urban, highly educated Romanian adults about internet use, mood, impulsivity, and work factors. Problematic internet use was linked to less perceived social support and work engagement, and more work addiction, anxiety, depression, and impulsivity; negative mood appeared to be a key indirect pathway.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace wellbeing and emotional state may be connected to unhealthy internet habits in adults.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether low mood or work stress makes you use the internet more than you intend.
ai.fact: Problematic internet use was positively associated with work addiction, depressive symptoms, trait anxiety, and impulsivity.

quiz.question: What did the study find about impulsivity alone as a pathway to problematic internet use?
quiz.answer: The indirect association through impulsivity alone was not significant.

ai.caveat: It was a cross-sectional survey, so it cannot show cause and effect or the order in which things happened.

items.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting

ai.headline: AI agents can match analyst earnings forecasts but their confidence intervals are often too narrow.
ai.summary: The study tested six AI models on forecasting US company earnings using filings, transcripts and news. Three models were no worse than analyst consensus, while three made larger errors. Across all models, their stated 80% prediction intervals captured actual earnings only 37% to 70% of the time, mostly because forecasts were too low.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI tools for financial forecasting may look reasonable on average but can still be overconfident about how uncertain their predictions are.
ai.life_skill: Treat any AI earnings forecast as uncertain and check whether it gives a realistic range rather than a single number.
ai.fact: EPSBench evaluates AI earnings forecasts across 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies.

quiz.question: How often did the AI models' stated 80% prediction intervals contain the actual reported EPS?
quiz.answer: Only 37% to 70% of the runs that returned an interval, with most misses above the upper bound because forecasts ran low.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and tests only six models on a fixed set of US firm-quarters, so the results may not generalise.

items.title: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months

ai.headline: A low-calorie diet and exercise program helped 54% of younger adults with type 2 diabetes achieve remission in six months.
ai.summary: Researchers studied younger adults with type 2 diabetes who followed an intensive low-calorie diet and structured exercise program. After six months, 54% achieved remission, compared with 4% who received usual care.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows that lifestyle changes may help some younger adults put type 2 diabetes into remission relatively quickly.
ai.life_skill: Talk to a qualified healthcare professional before making major changes to your diet or exercise routine if you have type 2 diabetes.
ai.fact: 54% of participants under age 45 in the intensive program achieved remission compared with 4% receiving usual care.

quiz.question: What percentage of younger adults in the intensive diet and exercise program achieved remission after six months?
quiz.answer: 54% achieved remission, compared with 4% receiving usual care.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the full peer-reviewed study, so the findings cannot yet be treated as proven.

items.title: How one of the body's own proteins drives the vicious cycle of inflammation in vaginal yeast infections

ai.headline: A body protein called albumin drives inflammation in vaginal yeast infections while protecting the fungus from immune attack.
ai.summary: The study looked at why immune responses to Candida albicans yeast infections can be intense and persistent. Researchers found that the host protein albumin fuels the inflammatory cascade and at the same time shields the fungal pathogen from the immune system.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why thrush symptoms can be severe and keep coming back, pointing toward new ways to treat recurrent infections.
ai.life_skill: If you keep getting thrush symptoms, see a GP or sexual health clinic rather than repeatedly treating yourself.
ai.fact: Up to three-quarters of women will experience a genital yeast infection at least once in their lives.

quiz.question: What does albumin do in vaginal yeast infections according to the study?
quiz.answer: It fuels the inflammatory cascade while shielding the fungal pathogen from the immune system.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a single study, not peer-reviewed evidence or proof that changing albumin will treat infections.

items.title: Crop diversification protects fields from extreme weather and boosts productivity

ai.headline: Diversifying crops and keeping soil covered helps farms survive extreme weather and produce more food.
ai.summary: Researchers in Brazil tested how varying crop rotations and maintaining constant soil vegetation affect farm resilience. They found these practices help protect crops from droughts and floods while also increasing overall productivity.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how farming methods can adapt to climate extremes helps explain how global food systems might stay stable in a changing world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how variety in your own routines or projects can make you more resilient to unexpected setbacks.
ai.fact: Keeping soil covered with vegetation is linked to better protection against both droughts and floods.

quiz.question: What two weather events does the study say these farming techniques help protect against?
quiz.answer: The techniques help protect crops against droughts and floods.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a specific regional study, so the results may not apply to all climates or farming systems.

items.title: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?

ai.headline: Crocodiles likely survived the dinosaur-extinction asteroid by staying in warm tropical refuges.

The strongest evidence supported sensory-adapted dental environments and audiovisual distraction or virtual reality, while music therapy had lower certainty; overall certainty ranged from very low to moderate because of bias, varied methods and imprecise results.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that simple, non-drug changes to the dental setting may help anxious children, though more high-quality research is needed before they become routine.
ai.life_skill: If a child feels anxious about dental visits, ask the dental team whether a calmer environment, headphones, music or a video could be used during treatment.
ai.fact: Dental anxiety affects an estimated 9%-20% of children and disproportionately impacts those with neurodevelopmental conditions.

quiz.question: Which sensory-based approaches had the strongest evidence for reducing children's dental anxiety and improving cooperation?
quiz.answer: Sensory-adapted dental environments and audiovisual distraction or virtual reality had moderate-certainty evidence, the strongest among the approaches reviewed.

ai.caveat: This is a systematic review of trials with overall low-to-moderate certainty, limited by risk of bias, heterogeneity and imprecise results, so it supports cautious use rather than proof of routine benefit.

items.title: Neonatal Sleep Disruption and Brain Development in Preterm Infants: A Narrative Review of Neurodevelopmental Outcomes

ai.headline: Sleep disruption in preterm babies may be linked to later brain and behaviour outcomes, but proof is limited.
ai.summary: The review looked at studies of preterm infants in neonatal intensive care and how noise, light, caregiving and painful procedures can disrupt sleep. It found that sleep disruption is linked to altered brain development, attention problems, attachment difficulties and stress system changes, though causes are hard to separate from prematurity and illness.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that protecting sleep in neonatal units could be a practical way to support long-term development in preterm babies.
ai.life_skill: Notice how noise, light and frequent handling might affect a baby’s sleep and consider quieter, clustered care where possible.
ai.fact: Sleep supports brain maturation, synaptic plasticity and white matter development in newborns.

quiz.question: What does the review say about the link between neonatal sleep disruption and later outcomes?
quiz.answer: It is linked to altered brain development, attention problems, attachment difficulties and stress system changes, but causal relationships remain difficult to establish.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review of observational studies and meta-analyses, not a randomised trial, so it cannot prove that sleep disruption causes later problems.

items.title: Maternity versus non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy.

ai.why_it_matters: It shows that there is currently no reliable evidence about whether the type of healthcare setting affects gestational diabetes screening and diagnosis.

quiz.answer: It found only one randomised trial with 781 participants.

items.title: Effect of virtual reality-based exergaming on multidimensional outcomes in individuals with cognitive impairment: a three-level meta-analysis based on the ICF framework

ai.headline: Virtual reality exercise games may improve thinking, movement and quality of life in people with cognitive impairment.
ai.summary: This review combined 22 randomised trials of virtual reality-based exergaming in people with cognitive impairment. quiz.question: Which outcome did the review find was not significantly improved by virtual reality exergaming?
quiz.answer: Depressive symptoms, comprehensive physical fitness and fall risk showed no significant effect.

ai.caveat: The included trials varied in quality and the evidence certainty was rated with GRADE, so the size of the benefit is not certain.

items.title: Problematic internet use among young people in Türkiye: a meta-analysis

ai.summary: This meta-analysis combined 27 studies of 16,488 high school and university students in Türkiye. ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how long someone spends online is more closely tied to problematic internet use than gender or family income.
ai.life_skill: Notice how many hours you spend online each day and consider whether that time is crowding out sleep, study, or face-to-face contact.
ai.fact: The gender gap in problematic internet use among young people in Türkiye was small and appeared to be getting smaller in more recent studies.

quiz.question: Which factor was most strongly linked to problematic internet use in this meta-analysis?
quiz.answer: Students in the longest daily internet-use category reported substantially higher problematic internet use than those in the shortest category.
