items.title: As effective as the teacher, but less motivating: a randomized controlled comparison of AI-generated and teacher feedback on students’ writing performance and intrinsic motivation

ai.headline: AI feedback improved writing as much as teacher feedback, but students felt less motivated by it.
ai.summary: A randomized trial compared AI-generated feedback, teacher feedback, and no feedback for undergraduate students revising essays. Both AI and teacher feedback led to better revised essays than no feedback, and were statistically equivalent to each other, but teacher feedback produced higher intrinsic motivation linked to feeling more related to the feedback source.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows AI can help improve written work at scale, while highlighting that human feedback still matters for motivation and connection.
ai.life_skill: Try using AI feedback to improve a draft, then ask a teacher or trusted person for encouragement and guidance.
ai.fact: AI-generated feedback and teacher feedback produced statistically equivalent improvements in revised-essay quality compared with no feedback.

quiz.question: Did AI-generated feedback and teacher feedback differ in how much they improved revised-essay quality?
quiz.answer: No, the two feedback conditions were statistically equivalent within the prespecified margin.

ai.caveat: The study was a single feedback-and-revision cycle at one institution, so results may not generalise to other settings or repeated cycles.

items.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables

ai.headline: A wearable-based AI coach made testable predictions for one cyclist over 18 months, with mixed results.
ai.summary: The study tested EpiCoach, an AI system that treats one athlete as an N-of-1 experiment, using heart rate, GPS and altitude data to predict future sessions and prescribe training. Over 18 months, its heart-rate forecasts beat standard methods, but its segment-time forecasts did not, and a safety officer vetoed its plan twice.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how personal health data could be used to make auditable, falsifiable predictions rather than unchecked recommendations.
ai.life_skill: Try recording your own predictions about how your body will respond before you change a habit, then check whether you were right.
ai.fact: The system’s heart-rate predictions were more accurate than standard forecasters, but its trail-segment time predictions were not.

quiz.question: Did EpiCoach’s predictions improve on standard forecasters for every outcome measured?
quiz.answer: No, it beat standard forecasters on heart rate but not on segment time.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on one athlete and has not been peer reviewed, so the results are not proof that the approach works for other people.

items.title: Green HRM, Green Leadership and Work Engagement in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Bibliometric–Systematic Review and Research Framework for Environmental Sustainability

ai.headline: AI can either help or harm green employee engagement at work, depending on how it is used.
ai.summary: A review of thousands of studies found that green HR practices, green leadership and work engagement are rarely studied together with AI. The few studies that do look at AI at employee level report mixed results: AI can act as a useful resource, but AI awareness can also lower green engagement through job stress or replace green leadership.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that new workplace technology does not automatically improve environmental efforts and can sometimes add stress or weaken leadership support.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether AI tools at work reduce your stress and support greener habits or add pressure and replace helpful leadership.
ai.fact: Only about 1% of the mapped documents examined green HRM, green leadership and employee engagement together, and only three also involved AI.

quiz.question: What did the few employee-level AI studies report about AI’s effect on green work engagement?
quiz.answer: They reported positive, null and negative effects, including AI awareness lowering green work engagement through job stress.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the AI findings come from only a small number of studies with mixed results.

items.title: Does autonomy enhance satisfaction, adherence and clinical outcomes? A Randomized Controlled Trial of a digital mental health intervention for college students

ai.headline: Letting students choose digital CBT topics did not improve satisfaction, adherence, or mental health outcomes versus a fixed lesson order.
ai.summary: A randomised trial assigned 575 college students to either a structured digital CBT programme or an autonomy-enhanced version where they could pick topics. Both groups reported similar satisfaction, adherence, and improvements in wellbeing, depression, anxiety, and quality of life after five weeks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that giving users topic choice in a digital mental health app may not add benefit over a set programme, which matters for how such tools are designed.
ai.life_skill: Try a structured digital mental health programme rather than worrying about choosing your own lesson order.
ai.fact: Participants in both versions of the digital CBT programme showed small-to-moderate improvements in mental wellbeing, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and quality of life from baseline to five weeks.

quiz.question: Did the autonomy-enhanced version outperform the structured version on satisfaction, adherence, or clinical outcomes?
quiz.answer: No, no significant differences were observed between the two conditions on those outcomes.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the study only compared two active versions rather than including an inactive control group.

items.title: Neuropsychiatric symptom clusters and plasma proteomic signatures across cognitive ageing and dementia in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo: a cross-sectional analysis of the EVCD-RDC cohort

ai.headline: In older adults in Kinshasa, certain blood proteins were linked to neuropsychiatric symptoms and depression scores.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 779 older adults with available blood protein data from a cohort of 1044 in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. They found that higher levels of NEFL, IL6, CCL13, and APOE protein were associated with greater symptom burden, depression scores, or nighttime behaviour, and identified three symptom dimensions.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how blood markers might one day help researchers understand mood and behaviour changes linked to ageing and dementia in under-studied populations.
ai.life_skill: Notice changes in mood, sleep, or behaviour in yourself or an older relative and discuss them with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Neuropsychiatric symptoms are common across cognitive ageing and dementia.

quiz.question: What type of study design was used in this analysis?
quiz.answer: It was a cross-sectional analysis of a cohort, meaning data were collected at one point in time.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and because it is observational and cross-sectional, it cannot show that the proteins cause the symptoms.

items.title: Nicotinic receptor in dopamine neurons mediates learned odor choice

ai.headline: A nicotinic receptor in fruit-fly reward neurons helps flies choose a learned odor when two odors compete.
ai.summary: Researchers studied fruit flies to see how a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor called Dα1 in dopamine neurons affects odor-sugar learning. Flies lacking Dα1 in these neurons had weaker odor-evoked signals and struggled to pick the rewarded odor when choosing between two odors, while their response to sugar and innate odor choices stayed intact.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how acetylcholine and dopamine interact in reward circuits to support value-based decisions when faced with competing options.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you are choosing between two familiar options and pause to check which one is actually linked to the better outcome.
ai.fact: In fruit flies, dopamine neurons in the PAM cluster convey sugar reward signals and promote approach toward a rewarded odor after associative learning.

quiz.question: What happened when Dα1 was knocked down in fruit-fly reward neurons?
quiz.answer: Odor-evoked synaptic signals were weakened and learned odor choice between two competing odors was impaired, while sugar responses and innate odor choice were largely preserved.

ai.caveat: The study was done in fruit flies, so the findings may not directly apply to humans.

items.title: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk

ai.headline: Daylight linked to lower dementia risk
ai.summary: Researchers studied daylight exposure in 87,000 adults and found higher exposure was associated with lower dementia risk. They discovered that less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily was a strong predictor of dementia. The study suggests a link between daylight and brain health.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding this link can help people take simple steps to reduce their dementia risk
ai.life_skill: Spend time outside during the day to get natural daylight
ai.fact: Higher daytime light exposure is associated with a lower risk of dementia

quiz.question: What was found to be a strong predictor of dementia?
quiz.answer: Getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily

ai.caveat: This study does not prove that daylight exposure directly reduces dementia risk, only that it is linked to it

items.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps

ai.headline: AI agents can learn to navigate live iPhone apps through online reinforcement learning with step-by-step feedback.
ai.summary: Researchers trained AI agents to navigate live iOS apps using an online reinforcement learning framework that splits tasks into planning and screen-grounding components. The agents received dense step-level feedback plus a terminal completion reward, and outperformed supervised fine-tuning and terminal-only RL baselines on iOS and Android benchmarks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how smaller AI models might become cheaper and more capable at everyday phone tasks without memorising fixed routes.
ai.life_skill: Try breaking a new phone task into small steps and checking progress after each one rather than only judging the final result.
ai.fact: The 8B reinforcement-learning agents achieved nearly a sevenfold improvement over the supervised fine-tuning baseline in out-of-distribution generalisation to Android environments.

quiz.question: What did the researchers use to give the AI agents feedback during training?
quiz.answer: They used an LLM-as-a-Judge to provide dense step-level feedback and a terminal reward for overall task completion.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Assessment and Treatment for Chronic Pain in Veterans With Serious Mental Illness

ai.headline: A trial is testing whether a talking therapy for pain works for veterans with serious mental illness.
ai.summary: The study looks at Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Chronic Pain in veterans who also have serious mental illness. It checks whether the therapy is practical and acceptable, and examines how pain and mental health symptoms affect each other.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights how chronic pain can block recovery and rehabilitation for people living with serious mental illness.
ai.life_skill: Notice how physical pain and low mood affect each other, and mention both to a healthcare professional.
ai.fact: Chronic pain is linked to poorer mental health and physical functioning in veterans with serious mental illness.

quiz.question: What is the study testing in veterans with serious mental illness?
quiz.answer: It is testing whether Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Chronic Pain is feasible and acceptable.

ai.caveat: This is a trial record with results posted, not a full peer-reviewed paper, so the findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: EPF/EPFL Peptide Signaling as a Regulatory Node Linking Stomatal Development to Drought and Heat Tolerance in Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.)

ai.headline: Tomato genes that shape leaf pores respond differently to drought and heat depending on the plant variety.
ai.summary: Researchers identified 15 EPF/EPFL genes in tomato that are linked to stomatal development and guard cell differentiation. Under drought, heat, or combined stress, five of these genes showed different activity patterns in two tomato varieties, suggesting genotype- and stress-dependent regulation.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how plants may cope with hotter and drier conditions, which matters for food security and understanding plant responses to climate stress.
ai.fact: Tomato has 15 EPF/EPFL family genes involved in stomatal complex development and guard cell differentiation.

quiz.question: What did the study find about EPF/EPFL gene activity in the two tomato varieties under stress?
quiz.answer: The genes showed distinct, genotype- and stress-dependent expression patterns under drought, heat, and combined drought-heat stress.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it reports gene-expression patterns rather than proof that these genes cause drought or heat tolerance.

items.title: Waves alter Antarctic polynyas by breaking up surrounding sea ice

ai.headline: Ocean waves help keep Antarctic polynyas open by breaking up nearby sea ice.
ai.summary: The study looked at polynyas, areas of open water surrounded by Antarctic sea ice. It found that waves breaking up surrounding sea ice play a role in maintaining these open-water areas alongside winds.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how Antarctic open-water areas form and stay open, which affects ocean-atmosphere exchange and marine life.
ai.fact: Polynyas are recurring areas of open water surrounded by sea ice that act as hot spots for sea-ice production and biological productivity.

quiz.question: What helps maintain Antarctic polynyas according to the study?
quiz.answer: Waves breaking up surrounding sea ice, along with powerful winds that push ice away from the coast.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the original peer-reviewed research, so the findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers

ai.headline: Blocking a cancer-related enzyme slowed tumour growth and extended survival in mice with different cancers.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a drug that inhibits METTL1, an enzyme involved in m7G methylation, in several mouse models of solid and blood cancers. The treatment impaired tumour growth and substantially prolonged survival across models of different tissue origin.
ai.why_it_matters: It points to a possible future approach for treating multiple cancer types, though it has only been tested in mice so far.
ai.fact: METTL1 is an m7G methyltransferase enzyme that can be pharmacologically inhibited to affect tumour growth in mice.

quiz.question: What effect did inhibiting METTL1 have in the mouse cancer models?
quiz.answer: It impaired tumour growth and substantially prolonged survival.

ai.caveat: The findings come from mouse models only, so they do not show the treatment would work or be safe in people.

items.title: Climate change threatens malaria elimination in the Asia Pacific

ai.headline: Climate change may threaten efforts to eliminate malaria in the Asia Pacific region.
ai.summary: A multidisciplinary group of policymakers and researchers discusses how climate change affects malaria in the Asia Pacific, identifies gaps in national adaptation strategies, and outlines five priority actions for the region.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how environmental changes can influence the spread of infectious diseases and the effectiveness of public health efforts.

quiz.question: What does the paper say climate change may threaten in the Asia Pacific?
quiz.answer: It may threaten malaria elimination in the region.

ai.caveat: The paper is a discussion by experts identifying gaps and priorities, not new experimental evidence or a randomised trial.

items.title: India caps mark-ups on 137 cancer drugs after court highlights 900% price difference

ai.headline: India caps trade mark-ups on 137 cancer drugs to make treatment more affordable.
ai.summary: India’s drug price regulator capped trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30% of their maximum retail price. An earlier analysis found average mark-ups on non-scheduled cancer drugs were around 170%, with some reaching 700% or more.
ai.why_it_matters: High medicine prices can push households into debt or put treatment out of reach, so price caps may affect what patients pay for cancer care.
ai.life_skill: Check whether your medicines are covered by government price controls before assuming the listed price is fixed.
ai.fact: India’s drug price regulator capped trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30% of their maximum retail price.

quiz.question: What did India cap on 137 cancer drugs?
quiz.answer: Trade margins were capped at 30% of their maximum retail price.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a policy change, not a research study measuring patient outcomes.

items.title: Revealing the benefit of eye motion for acuity under emulated cone loss

ai.headline: Tiny eye movements help people see clearly even when many cone cells are inactive.
ai.summary: Researchers used a system to mimic cone cell loss in healthy eyes by switching off stimulation to selected cones. They found that visual acuity gets worse as more cones are lost, but natural eye movements partly compensate by letting the remaining cones gather more information from what is being viewed.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why vision can stay surprisingly good despite retinal disease and shows how ordinary eye movements support sight.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your eyes make tiny movements when you look at something, and let them move naturally rather than staring rigidly.
ai.fact: Clinically normal visual acuity can persist despite up to 50% of cone cells being lost.

quiz.question: What did eye motion do for visual acuity under cone dropout?
quiz.answer: It provided a compensatory benefit, making acuity at the highest dropout level equivalent to a static condition with nearly twice as many sampling elements.

ai.caveat: The study emulated cone loss in healthy eyes using stimulation rather than studying actual retinal degeneration, so it may not fully reflect real disease.

items.title: Ratings, Debt, and Deficits: An Exploration -- by Olivier J. Blanchard, Daniel Leigh, Prachi Mishra

ai.headline: Debt affects sovereign credit ratings
ai.summary: Researchers studied the effects of debt and primary fiscal balances on sovereign credit ratings using a simple model. They found that ratings give more weight to debt than forecast primary balances and understate the effects of interest rate and growth rate differences. The model's implications differ from actual ratings in several ways.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how debt affects credit ratings can inform decisions about government borrowing and spending
ai.life_skill: Check how debt and interest rates affect your own credit score
ai.fact: Sovereign credit ratings are influenced by debt and primary fiscal balances

quiz.question: What do sovereign credit ratings give more weight to?
quiz.answer: Debt relative to forecast primary balances

ai.caveat: This is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution

items.title: Passive tobacco smoke exposure linked to nonallergic atopic dermatitis severity in young children

ai.headline: Passive tobacco smoke exposure is linked to more severe nonallergic eczema in young children.
ai.summary: The study looked at children aged 0 to 2 years with nonallergic atopic dermatitis. It found that passive tobacco smoke exposure, especially paternal smoking and exposure after birth in the household, was associated with increased disease severity.
ai.why_it_matters: This suggests that reducing children's exposure to tobacco smoke at home may be relevant to managing early childhood eczema.
ai.life_skill: Try to keep babies and toddlers away from tobacco smoke at home.
ai.fact: Passive tobacco smoke exposure is associated with increased severity of nonallergic atopic dermatitis in children aged 0 to 2 years.

quiz.question: What was passive tobacco smoke exposure linked to in children aged 0 to 2 years with nonallergic atopic dermatitis?
quiz.answer: It was associated with increased disease severity.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study reported in a news article, so it shows a link rather than proving that smoke exposure causes worse eczema.

items.title: A soft robot could help doctors diagnose and treat disorders of the small intestine

ai.headline: MIT engineers created a soft robotic enteroscope to reach the small intestine for biopsies and drug delivery.
ai.summary: MIT engineers designed a robotic enteroscope that can inch through the hard-to-reach small intestine. The device aims to make biopsies and drug delivery easier.
ai.why_it_matters: It could make diagnosing and treating small intestine disorders simpler and less invasive in the future.

quiz.question: What did MIT engineers design according to the article?
quiz.answer: They designed a robotic enteroscope that can inch through the hard-to-reach small intestine.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about engineering research, not a peer-reviewed study with patient results.

items.title: ‘Reverse physics’ could help bridge the classical and quantum worlds

ai.headline: Some physicists are trying to build the laws of physics from mathematics rather than starting with observations.
ai.summary: The article describes an effort called 'reverse physics' that aims to rebuild the laws of physics starting from mathematics, instead of the usual approach of observing the world first and then finding the maths to explain it.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how new ways of thinking about science might one day help connect our everyday world with the strange rules of quantum physics.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you assume something is true just because you have seen it happen, and consider whether there might be a deeper pattern behind it.
ai.fact: Physics usually begins with observations and develops mathematics to support them later.

quiz.question: What does 'reverse physics' aim to do differently?
quiz.answer: It aims to rebuild the laws of physics from mathematics up, rather than starting from observations.

ai.caveat: This is a news column describing an idea, not a research study with tested results.

items.title: South West Water given lowest environmental rating

ai.headline: South West Water received the lowest environmental rating from the Environment Agency.
ai.summary: The Environment Agency assessed South West Water’s environmental performance and found it is performing significantly below target for pollution.
ai.why_it_matters: Water company pollution affects local rivers, beaches and the environment people use every day.
ai.life_skill: Check the Environment Agency’s ratings for your water company to see how it performs on pollution.
ai.fact: South West Water was given the lowest environmental rating by the Environment Agency.

quiz.question: What rating did the Environment Agency give South West Water?
quiz.answer: It gave the firm the lowest environmental rating.

ai.caveat: This is a single news report, not a peer-reviewed study, so it cannot establish causes or broader patterns.

items.title: Who wrote that paper? AI use spurs debate over scientific authorship

ai.headline: AI-written research papers are sparking debate over who should be credited as an author.
ai.summary: A news report from Science describes growing discussion about how credit and responsibility should be assigned when artificial intelligence helps write scientific papers. Existing authorship rules may need updating to reflect AI's role.
ai.why_it_matters: It affects how much trust we can place in research findings and who is held accountable if something is wrong.
ai.life_skill: Check who is listed as an author on any article you read and consider whether AI may have helped write it.
ai.fact: Scientific journals and researchers are debating new rules for crediting AI contributions to papers.

quiz.question: What does the report say may need updating because of AI-written papers?
quiz.answer: The rules governing credit and responsibility for machine-written papers may need a reboot.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a research study, so it offers no data or tested conclusions.

items.title: Effects of structured exercise on executive function across childhood, adolescence, and later life: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis examining exercise skill characteristics.

ai.headline: Structured exercise is linked to better executive function on average, but benefits are not uniform across people or programs.
ai.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 47 randomised trials with 4,195 participants looked at structured exercise and executive function in children, adolescents, and older adults. Exercise was associated with a small-to-moderate average improvement across inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility, but effects varied widely and no specific program feature reliably produced larger gains.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests staying active may support thinking skills at different ages, but there is no evidence yet for one best type or dose of exercise.
ai.life_skill: Try including regular structured physical activity in your week as part of a balanced routine.
ai.fact: Structured exercise was associated with better executive-function performance on average across children, adolescents, and older adults.

quiz.question: Did the review find that one specific exercise feature reliably produced larger improvements in executive function?
quiz.answer: No, it found no specific executive-function domain, developmental stage, program duration, comparator type, or broadly defined exercise skill characteristic that reliably yielded larger effects.

ai.caveat: The evidence was rated low certainty because of serious risk of bias and inconsistency, and publication bias remained uncertain.

items.title: Impact of Daily Screen and Social Media Time on REM Sleep in Adolescents
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

ai.headline: In a small pilot study, screen and social media time were not clearly linked to REM sleep in five adolescent athletes.
ai.summary: Researchers tracked five adolescent cross-country athletes for 90 nights using smartwatches and phone screen-time data. They found no statistically significant link between daily screen or social media use and total sleep, REM minutes, or REM percentage.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that common worries about screens stealing REM sleep are not yet proven, especially in small studies.
ai.life_skill: Notice how you feel after different amounts of screen time before bed rather than assuming screens always harm your sleep.
ai.fact: REM sleep is important for memory consolidation and emotional processing.

quiz.question: Did the study find a significant link between screen time and REM sleep?
quiz.answer: No, the correlations between screen time and REM sleep were small and not statistically significant.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not peer reviewed, with only five participants and 90 nights, so it was underpowered to detect anything but large effects.

items.title: Models and components of investigation and bereavement care after sudden and unexpected child death: a scoping review.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: A review will map how families are supported after a child dies suddenly and unexpectedly.
ai.summary: This is a protocol for a planned Cochrane review. It will identify and describe models and components of investigation and bereavement care for families in high-income countries after the sudden and unexpected death of a child aged seven days to under 18 years.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps us understand how services are organised and delivered to support grieving families.

quiz.question: What kind of document is this paper?
quiz.answer: It is a protocol for a planned Cochrane review, not a completed review with findings.

ai.caveat: This is only a protocol describing what the review plans to do; it does not report any findings yet.

items.title: Early cardiac lipid overload, redox-inflammatory imbalance, fibrotic remodeling, and cannabinoid receptor up-regulation in sucrose-rich diet-fed rats: preventive effects of full-spectrum cannabis oil

ai.headline: Sugar diet harms heart health
ai.summary: Researchers studied the effects of a sucrose-rich diet on rats' heart health and the potential benefits of full-spectrum cannabis oil. They found that the sugar diet led to increased blood pressure, cardiac injury markers, and lipid accumulation. Cannabis oil prevented or reduced these negative effects.
ai.why_it_matters: This study's findings could have implications for understanding how sugar intake affects heart health and potential preventive measures.
ai.life_skill: Try to limit your daily sugar intake to protect your heart health.
ai.fact: Excessive sugar consumption is linked to metabolic disease.

quiz.question: What was the effect of full-spectrum cannabis oil on sugar diet-induced heart damage in rats?
quiz.answer: It prevented or markedly attenuated most of the negative effects.

ai.caveat: This study was conducted on rats and its findings may not be directly applicable to humans.

items.title: Generative artificial intelligence and terminology work: structural associations of prompt strategy preference, cognitive load, and self-efficacy

ai.headline: People who prefer structured AI prompts report lower mental effort, partly through greater confidence using AI.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 1,760 practitioners who use large language models for terminology work. Those who preferred structured prompt strategies reported lower subjective cognitive load, and this link was partly explained by higher AI interaction self-efficacy. Three user profiles emerged, with high strategy users showing the lowest cognitive load and highest self-efficacy, regardless of career stage.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how the way people interact with AI tools can shape their mental effort and confidence in knowledge work.
ai.life_skill: Try structuring your prompts before asking an AI for help with precise wording or definitions.
ai.fact: Prompt strategy preference, AI interaction self-efficacy, and subjective cognitive load are structurally linked in terminology work using generative AI.

quiz.question: What did the study find about people who preferred structured prompt strategies?
quiz.answer: They reported lower subjective cognitive load, partly explained by higher AI interaction self-efficacy.

ai.caveat: The findings come from a single cross-sectional survey, so they show associations rather than prove cause and effect.

items.title: Comparing Human Role-Players and LLM-Simulated Clients in Online Counselling Training: An Analysis of Counselling Patterns

ai.headline: LLM-simulated clients can mimic human role-players in counselling training, with some differences in communication patterns.
ai.summary: Researchers compared novice counsellors practising with human peers acting as clients against practising with an LLM-simulated client. They analysed sentence-level counselling communication patterns and found both similarities and differences between the two settings, suggesting LLM role-play may help build counselling skills but needs refinement.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could offer accessible practice for people learning supportive communication skills.
ai.life_skill: Try practising difficult conversations with a trusted person or a reputable simulation before facing them in real life.
ai.fact: LLM-simulated clients produced counselling communication patterns that were both similar to and different from human role-players.

quiz.question: What did the study compare?
quiz.answer: It compared novice counsellors interacting with human role-players versus an LLM-simulated client.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Noise as a global change driver: a meta-analysis of its fitness consequences for birds

ai.headline: Human-made noise reduces birds' fitness, especially when they are young and exposed to realistic noise.
ai.summary: Researchers combined results from 53 experiments on 45 bird species to see how human-made noise affects fitness. Overall, noise exposure reduced fitness across different measures, with stronger effects before fledging and when the noise sounded realistic rather than synthetic.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows noise pollution is a serious environmental pressure that can affect wildlife survival and reproduction, not just behaviour.
ai.life_skill: Notice how human-made noise affects the animals around you and consider quieter choices where practical.
ai.fact: Experimental studies show anthropogenic noise can reduce avian fitness independently of other environmental stressors.

quiz.question: When were the negative effects of noise on bird fitness strongest?
quiz.answer: Effects were stronger when exposure occurred before fledging and when the noise was ecologically realistic.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed.

items.title: Growing Well with Grow It!: Acceptability of a Gamified mHealth App for Adolescents With a Chronic Somatic Illness – A Mixed Methods Study

ai.headline: App helps teens with chronic illness
ai.summary: The Grow It! app was studied for its acceptability among adolescents with chronic somatic illnesses. The app received a positive overall rating and helped participants recognise their emotions. Participants suggested improvements to the app's design and functionality.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it shows how mobile health apps can support the well-being of teenagers with chronic illnesses
ai.life_skill: Try using mobile health apps to track and manage your emotions
ai.fact: Over 17% of children live with a chronic somatic illness

quiz.question: What percentage of children live with a chronic somatic illness?
quiz.answer: Over 17% of children live with a chronic somatic illness

ai.caveat: This is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution

items.title: Formative Evaluation to Inform Recruitment and Engagement Strategies for emergency activation of blood donors in Nimba County, Liberia

ai.headline: In Liberia, family replacement and paid blood donors are motivated by altruism and family duty but face distance, cost and health worries.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 12 blood donors in Nimba County, Liberia, who had donated in the past year. Most were men who had donated both as family replacement and paid donors. They said altruism, good past experiences and helping family encouraged donation, while distance, testing concerns and costs put people off; many worried about health effects but thought community outreach could recruit new donors.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how emergency blood supplies in low-resource areas rely on informal donor networks and what might help or hinder them.
ai.life_skill: Notice who donates blood in your community and what makes it easier or harder for them to do so.
ai.fact: About 36.6% of blood donations in low-income countries come from family replacement or paid donors.

quiz.question: What did donors in the study say would be an effective way to recruit new blood donors?
quiz.answer: They believed outreach at community institutions would be an effective way to recruit new donors.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on interviews with only 12 donors in one Liberian county, so the findings are not peer-reviewed and may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Leptospirosis occurs as frequently as malaria among adolescent and adult acute febrile patients in Hoima, Uganda: A prospective health facility-based study

ai.headline: Leptospirosis is as common as malaria among fever patients in Hoima, Uganda.
ai.summary: Researchers tested 330 adolescents and adults with acute fever at two health facilities in Hoima, Uganda, for leptospirosis and malaria. About one in three patients had leptospirosis, a rate comparable to malaria, and nearly 9% had both infections.

ai.life_skill: Notice how visible symbols in your community might reinforce certain expectations or norms.
ai.fact: Social norms can persist and influence behaviour even after the formal authority that enforced them is removed.

quiz.question: Where were the increases in female employment and schooling largest?
quiz.answer: The increases were largest in areas where no religious monument survived the ban.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on a historical natural experiment, so it shows a link rather than proving that removing symbols directly causes norm changes.

items.title: Spinal cord injury can reshape gut microbes that influence whole-body health

ai.headline: Spinal cord injuries may change gut bacteria, which could affect overall body health and healing.
ai.summary: Researchers examined the genetic makeup of gut microbes in people with spinal cord injuries. They found early signs that these microbial changes are linked to inflammation and immune function, suggesting they might play a role in the healing process.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that an injury to the spine can have effects far beyond the nervous system, influencing the internal ecosystem that supports general health.
ai.life_skill: Notice that physical health issues can sometimes have unexpected connections to other body systems, like digestion.
ai.fact: Gut microbial communities can be reshaped by spinal cord injuries, potentially influencing whole-body inflammation.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest about the relationship between spinal cord injuries and gut microbes?
quiz.answer: The study suggests that spinal cord injuries can reshape gut microbes, which may influence inflammation and immune function.

items.title: In Dark Eden, I imagined how life might exist on a sunless planet

ai.headline: A science-fiction author explains how he imagined life on a sunless rogue planet outside the Milky Way.

quiz.answer: A rogue planet outside the Milky Way with no sun.

items.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Deep learning can help diagnose brain diseases from EEG scans, but is not yet ready for routine clinics.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined studies using deep learning to analyse EEG brain recordings for diagnosing neurological diseases. ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI may one day support faster, more objective diagnosis of brain disorders from routine EEG tests.

quiz.question: Which brain diseases does the review say deep-learning EEG models may help diagnose?

ai.caveat: The review summarises existing research rather than providing new clinical proof, and the authors note that translating these models into everyday medical practice remains difficult.

items.title: Impact of COVID-19 on adolescent mental health in Albania

ai.headline: In Albania, girls and older teenagers reported worse mental health impacts from the pandemic than boys or younger peers.
ai.summary: This study surveyed over 5,000 Albanian adolescents aged 11–15 in 2022 about their mental health during the pandemic. It found that roughly 35% reported a negative impact, with girls and older teenagers significantly more likely to report this than boys or younger students.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that mental health struggles during crises are not evenly distributed, suggesting that support systems need to specifically address the needs of older adolescents and girls.
ai.life_skill: Notice that stress affects different people differently, and check in with friends to see if they are struggling even if they seem fine.
ai.fact: In this Albanian study, family wealth and whether parents were employed did not predict whether adolescents reported negative mental health impacts from the pandemic.

quiz.question: Which two groups of Albanian adolescents were most likely to report negative mental health impacts from COVID-19?
quiz.answer: Girls and older adolescents were significantly more likely to perceive negative mental health impact.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional study relying on self-reported data, so it cannot prove causation or account for changes in mental health over time.

items.title: Quality of life among vocational rehabilitation patients with mild work-related disability and its association with return-to-work outcomes

ai.headline: Better quality of life after rehabilitation is linked to a higher chance of returning to work for injured employees.
ai.summary: A study followed 343 employees with mild work-related disability who received vocational rehabilitation. Their health-related quality of life improved in several areas, and those who returned to work—either to their original job or a new one—reported better quality-of-life scores at discharge than those who did not return.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that feeling healthier and more capable after an injury may be linked to getting back into work.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your confidence about returning to work changes as your health improves, and discuss any concerns with your rehabilitation team.
ai.fact: Better quality of life at discharge is positively associated with return-to-work outcomes after vocational rehabilitation.

quiz.question: What did the study find about quality-of-life scores at discharge for people who returned to work compared with those who did not?
quiz.answer: People who returned to their original post or a new post had significantly higher quality-of-life scores in several areas than those who did not return to work.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study from one hospital, so it cannot prove that better quality of life causes a return to work.

items.title: Early career challenges of physical education teachers

ai.headline: New PE teachers face location, training and support challenges in their first five years.
ai.summary: This study interviewed 25 physical education teachers in Türkiye within their first five years of teaching. It found they struggled with local climate, transport and culture, felt unprepared for administration, classroom management and assessment due to a theory-practice gap in training, and lacked support from administrators, students and parents.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that new teachers’ success depends on both personal resources and workplace support, not just individual effort.
ai.life_skill: Notice which parts of a new job feel hardest and ask a trusted colleague or mentor for specific help.
ai.fact: Early-career physical education teachers in Türkiye report adaptation difficulties linked to geographic, pedagogical and social factors.

quiz.question: What three main themes did the study find in early-career PE teachers’ challenges?
quiz.answer: Regional and psychosocial dynamics, PETE and perceived professional competence, and stakeholder relationships and perceived social support.

ai.caveat: This is a small qualitative case study in one country, so its findings are not proof and may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Multistep and Multivariate Time Series Explainability with GradientSHAP: A Wind Power Case Study

ai.headline: A new method helps explain AI wind power forecasts by showing which weather factors matter most.
ai.summary: The study adapted a technique called GradientSHAP to make AI models for predicting wind power easier to understand. It found that, with careful handling and expert knowledge, the method can reveal how environmental and site-specific factors influence forecasts across multiple time steps.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how AI predicts wind power can help grid operators manage renewable energy more reliably as the world moves away from fossil fuels.
ai.life_skill: Try asking how an AI tool reaches its conclusion before trusting its recommendation.
ai.fact: Wind power is variable and intermittent, which creates challenges for integrating it into electricity grids.

quiz.question: What did the researchers adapt GradientSHAP to do in this study?
quiz.answer: They adapted it to provide interpretability for multivariate, multistep wind power forecasting.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet established.

items.title: Eye See Your Intentions: Age-Related Differences in Gaze Perception and Trustworthiness Attributions

ai.headline: Older adults are more likely to see averted gaze as direct and rate those faces as more trustworthy.
ai.summary: Researchers tested 307 adults aged 18 to 88 online using faces with different expressions and gaze directions. As age increased, people were more likely to perceive averted gaze as direct, especially for non-fearful expressions, and greater perceived direct gaze was linked to higher trustworthiness ratings, particularly among older adults.
ai.why_it_matters: This may help explain why older adults sometimes place greater trust in others and could be more vulnerable to deception.
ai.life_skill: Notice where someone’s eyes are actually pointing before deciding whether they seem trustworthy.
ai.fact: Direct gaze is generally interpreted as an approach signal, while averted gaze is interpreted as an avoidance signal.

quiz.question: What happened to trustworthiness ratings as perceived direct gaze increased?
quiz.answer: Greater perception of direct gaze was associated with greater facial trustworthiness attributions.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the online design cannot prove that age causes these differences in gaze perception or trust judgments.

items.title: Synthetic Reception: Manufacturing the Signals of Uptake in Hype and Technology Expectations

ai.headline: Companies can secretly fake signs that lots of people like a new technology to make it seem popular.
ai.summary: The paper studies how hype is created not just by promises but by how audiences receive them. It introduces “synthetic reception,” where producers hide their own role in creating signals of uptake—such as likes, early reactions or endorsements—so they look like independent audience judgements.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people question whether apparent public excitement about a new app, device or trend is genuine or manufactured.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether excitement about a new technology comes from many independent voices or looks like a coordinated campaign.
ai.fact: Signals of uptake such as counts, first reactions and endorsements shape what audiences decide deserves attention.

quiz.question: What does “synthetic reception” fake?
quiz.answer: It fakes the independence of a signal of uptake, making a producer’s concealed contribution look like independent audience judgement.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and offers a conceptual framework rather than tested evidence.

items.title: Quantifying Localized Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes by Deep Learning on H&E Images: Analytical Validation and Prognostic Value in Lung Adenocarcinoma

ai.headline: An AI tool that maps immune cells in lung cancer tissue may predict survival better than current tests.
ai.summary: Researchers developed an AI method called the focal TIL score that measures immune cell density in specific areas of lung cancer tissue using standard pathology images. In a study of 685 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, higher focal TIL scores were linked to longer overall survival and outperformed the standard PD-L1 biomarker.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could make cancer prognosis more objective and standardised using images hospitals already produce.

quiz.question: What did the focal TIL score measure in lung cancer tissue?
quiz.answer: It measured the density of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes within specific tiles across the tissue region.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the survival finding comes from an observational association rather than a randomised trial.

items.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD

ai.headline: Academia can suit early-career academics with ADHD, but institutional pressures often block that potential.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed early-career academics with ADHD about their work experiences. They found that ADHD traits can bring strengths such as curiosity and exploration, but social and institutional pressures often make it harder to thrive. The study argues that both individual careers and collective knowledge production can benefit when universities include and support neurodivergent academics.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace context shapes whether neurodivergent traits help or hinder people at work.
ai.life_skill: Notice which work settings help you focus and which create friction, and consider asking for adjustments that suit your needs.
ai.fact: ADHD traits can include both challenges, such as time management, and strengths, such as curiosity-driven exploration.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest about academia for early-career academics with ADHD?
quiz.answer: Academia can be rewarding for them, but social and institutional pressures often inhibit that potential.

ai.caveat: This is a small interview-based study, so its findings cannot be generalised to all academics with ADHD or proven to apply universally.

items.title: 128,000-year-old ice in Tibet could rewrite climate history

ai.headline: Ancient ice found in Tibet
ai.summary: Scientists discovered ancient ice in Tibet that may be over 128,000 years old, preserving a record of Earth's climate. ai.life_skill: Explore how climate change affects your local environment.
ai.fact: Ancient ice in Tibet may be over 128,000 years old.

items.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

ai.headline: One AI model can both rerank search results and generate answers, saving memory and time.
ai.summary: The study tested Glance, a system that lets a single 9-billion-parameter AI model score and rerank retrieved passages using a lightweight adapter instead of running a separate reranking model. On two retrieval datasets it matched or beat a strong reranker, and on 300 HotpotQA questions it improved answer quality by a small but statistically supported margin.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI search tools could become faster and cheaper to run by using one model for several jobs instead of many.
ai.life_skill: Try checking whether an AI answer cites its sources before trusting it.
ai.fact: Glance achieved nDCG@10 of 0.741 on SciFact and 0.345 on NFCorpus, compared with 0.721 and 0.326 for bge-reranker-v2-m3.

quiz.question: What did Glance use to score candidate passages without prefilling each pair separately?
quiz.answer: A lightweight decision adapter and pointer head branching from a shared cached context.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and evaluation covers only two retrieval datasets, one QA dataset and one backbone family.

items.title: Impact Of Early Cognitive Rehabilitation On Functional Outcomes Following Moderate Traumatic Brain Injury

ai.summary: This study examined the impact of early cognitive rehabilitation on patients with moderate traumatic brain injury. The study aimed to detect the effect of this rehabilitation on functional outcomes. The results of the study are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.

ai.life_skill: Try seeking professional help for brain injuries
ai.fact: Cognitive rehabilitation is used to aid recovery from traumatic brain injuries

items.title: A new neural code for position: generalizable spatial maps in mouse medial frontal cortex

ai.headline: Mouse frontal cortex cells may encode position using distances to landmarks, helping navigation.
ai.summary: Researchers imaged brain cells in mice exploring a square arena with landmarks. Activity in the medial frontal cortex could predict the animal’s position even in areas where the model was not trained, unlike cells in the hippocampus or orbitofrontal cortex. A model based on squared distance to multiple landmarks explained this pattern.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a way the brain might generalise known locations to plan routes through new spaces.

items.title: New travel tool combines three algorithms to tailor destination recommendations

ai.summary: The paper describes a new tourist recommendation system that combines three algorithms to match destinations to travelers’ preferences, budgets and travel routes. It aims to fix a limitation of digital platforms that often prioritise popularity over practical considerations.

quiz.answer: It combines three algorithms to match destinations to preferences, budgets and travel routes.

items.title: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

ai.headline: Wearable-guided remote cardiac rehab may boost fitness and activity, but results are inconsistent across settings.
ai.summary: This systematic review of 18 randomised trials looked at wrist-worn wearable-guided cardiac rehabilitation delivered fully remotely or in hybrid form for people with cardiovascular disease. It found average improvements in peak oxygen uptake, six-minute walk distance and daily steps, but prediction intervals included no effect, meaning benefits may not hold in every future setting.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how remote, wearable-supported rehab could help more people with heart disease stay active outside clinic-based programmes.
ai.life_skill: Try using a wrist-worn activity tracker to monitor your daily steps and set gradual movement goals if you are managing a heart condition, after checking with your healthcare team.
ai.fact: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the consistency of benefits across future settings?
quiz.answer: The prediction intervals included no effect, indicating uncertainty about whether benefits will be consistent in comparable future settings.

items.title: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence in early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections: Systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: AI models show promising early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viruses, but evidence is uneven and biased.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 43 studies on artificial intelligence for early diagnosis of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Reported accuracy and other performance measures were high, but most studies were at high risk of bias, focused on dengue in Asia, and lacked external validation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows AI could one day help spot these infections sooner, but current results are not yet reliable enough for routine use everywhere.
ai.life_skill: Check that any health app or AI diagnostic tool you use has been independently tested and validated before trusting its results.
ai.fact: Most AI studies for early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections focused on dengue and were conducted in Asia.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the quality of the AI studies?
quiz.answer: Most studies were at high overall risk of bias, and calibration and external validation were uncommon.

ai.caveat: The pooled results are descriptive summaries of a highly heterogeneous evidence base, not proof of real-world performance.

items.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID syndrome: a scoping review of current evidence in adults

ai.headline: Sleep apnoea may be linked to long COVID, but the direction and cause are still unclear.
ai.summary: A scoping review of 11 studies looked at adults with obstructive sleep apnoea and long COVID. It found an association between the two, with symptoms such as fatigue, breathing problems, cognitive difficulties and cardiovascular issues reported, but the nature and direction of the link vary across studies.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that sleep health could matter for recovery after COVID-19, though more research is needed before firm conclusions can be drawn.
ai.life_skill: Notice how well you sleep and discuss ongoing tiredness or breathing problems with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Obstructive sleep apnoea involves interrupted breathing during sleep and can cause sleep fragmentation and low oxygen levels.

quiz.answer: It found an association between them, but the direction and causality remain uncertain.

items.title: What Helps or Hinders Therapeutic Relationships in Inpatient Mental Healthcare: a Systematic Review to Inform Policy and Practice

ai.headline: Staff empathy, consistent time together, shared power and welcoming ward spaces help build good therapeutic relationships on mental health wards.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 184 studies involving nearly 20,000 people to see what helps or harms relationships between staff and service users on inpatient mental health wards. It found that reducing power imbalances, staff showing empathy and treating people as individuals, having consistent staff with time to connect, and ward environments that allow interaction all support positive relationships, while restrictive practices and task-focused, risk-focused ward cultures weaken them.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday interactions and ward environments shape the quality of care people receive when they are most vulnerable.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether staff treat you as an individual rather than just a patient, and ask for time to talk if you feel rushed.
ai.fact: Therapeutic relationships between service users and staff on inpatient mental health wards are central to high-quality care.

quiz.question: What did the review find helps build positive relationships on inpatient mental health wards?
quiz.answer: Staff relational skills such as empathy and non-judgemental approaches, staff continuity and time to connect, reduced power imbalances, and ward environments that create opportunities for interaction.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it synthesises many different study designs rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: Familial factors inflate the estimated effects of genetic liability to ADHD on behavioural outcomes

ai.headline: Family background may explain much of the harm linked to ADHD, not ADHD itself.
ai.summary: Researchers compared population-wide results with results from siblings to separate a person’s own ADHD from shared family factors. ai.fact: Genetic liability to ADHD is linked to several health and behavioural outcomes in population studies, but those links weaken when family factors are accounted for.

quiz.question: What happened to the estimated effect of ADHD genetic liability on depressive symptoms when researchers compared siblings instead of the whole population?
quiz.answer: It fell from 0.059 SD to 0.002 SD, suggesting little or no direct effect once family factors were considered.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Beyond social skills: emotion regulation as a potential mechanism linking physical exercise to social anxiety in left-behind adolescents

ai.headline: Physical exercise is linked to lower social anxiety in left-behind adolescents, partly through emotion regulation.
ai.summary: The study looked at 862 left-behind adolescents in China and found that more physical exercise was linked to less social anxiety. items.title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations

ai.headline: Most AI agents tested could not run vending machines as profitably as a simple rule-based system.
ai.summary: Researchers created a simulated benchmark where AI agents managed 20 vending machines across five site types for 180 days, handling ordering, inventory, costs and expiry. ai.life_skill: Before trusting an AI tool to manage money or stock, check whether its results beat a simple, low-cost rule over time.
ai.fact: AI agents can struggle to turn good individual decisions into sustained economic returns when physical costs and inventory expiry are involved.

quiz.question: How did most of the AI agents perform compared with the rule-based baseline?
quiz.answer: Four of the five AI agents earned lower returns than the rule-based inventory-control baseline.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on a simulated benchmark, not peer-reviewed evidence from real vending operations.

items.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning

ai.headline: A small AI model can improve its own financial reasoning by fixing just its first mistake, without a stronger teacher.
ai.summary: The study tested Fin-SD, a method where a student AI spots its first wrong step on a failed finance problem, writes a short critique, and retrains itself starting just before that error. On a custom multi-step financial reasoning benchmark, it improved accuracy by 3.03 percentage points over the base model, matched full self-distillation while using 9.5% fewer tokens, and showed no clear drop in general reasoning or compliance metrics.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that targeted self-correction can boost step-by-step reasoning without needing a bigger or external model, which matters for understanding how AI systems might improve locally and privately.
ai.life_skill: When you get a multi-step problem wrong, go back to the first step where it went off track and redo from there rather than starting over.
ai.fact: Fin-SD matched on-policy self-distillation from full reference solutions on accuracy while generating 9.5% fewer tokens.

quiz.question: What did the study find about replacing the specific critique with generic feedback?
quiz.answer: It matched Fin-SD’s entire accuracy gain, suggesting the benefit comes from where supervision is applied rather than the hint content.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, tested on one model family and a custom benchmark, so the results are not yet established proof.

ai.summary: AI has made scientific discoveries, but its accuracy is now being questioned by mathematicians. This has sparked a debate about the reliability of AI in science. The debate is ongoing and its implications are being explored.

ai.life_skill: Check the sources of scientific information to ensure reliability.

quiz.answer: Its accuracy is being questioned.

ai.headline: King's Observatory for sale
ai.summary: The King's Observatory in London is up for sale, it was built for King George III to watch the 1769 transit of Venus. The observatory has an asking price of £18 million. It is a historic site with potential for new ownership.

ai.fact: The King's Observatory was built to observe the 1769 transit of Venus.

quiz.question: Why was the King's Observatory built?

items.title: Capturing the complete process of embryonic development

ai.headline: Mice embryonic development mapped
ai.summary: Researchers tracked over 1 million cells to study embryonic development in mice. They created a detailed map of this process. This map could provide insights into development and disease.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding embryonic development can provide insights into human health and disease
ai.fact: Embryonic development in mice has been mapped in detail

quiz.question: What was mapped in detail by researchers?

items.title: Immunometabolic Memory in Obesity: Nutritional Drivers, Persistence, and Reversibility

ai.headline: Obesity leaves lasting immune changes that weight loss doesn't fully reverse, and no diet erases them.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed evidence on whether obesity causes persistent immune system changes and if nutrition can reverse them. They found obesity creates lasting immune memory across multiple body systems, weight loss doesn't fully normalize these changes, and no dietary pattern has been proven to erase this memory in humans.
ai.why_it_matters: Past obesity may have long-term immune consequences even after weight loss, and simply dieting may not undo these changes.
ai.fact: Obesity can cause persistent epigenetic changes in immune cells that remain after weight loss.

quiz.question: Does any dietary pattern erase established obesity-associated immune memory in humans?
quiz.answer: No dietary pattern has been shown to erase established obesity-associated immune memory in humans.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review, not a systematic review, and human data on reversal of immune memory after weight loss are absent.

items.title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.

ai.headline: Valves help children with air leaks
ai.summary: Researchers studied the use of endobronchial valves in children with persistent air leaks or bronchopleural fistulas. They found that valve placement can improve air-leak symptoms in selected children. However, the evidence is limited due to small sample sizes and retrospective designs.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it could provide a new treatment option for children with severe respiratory complications
ai.life_skill: Consult a doctor about new treatments for respiratory issues
ai.fact: Endobronchial valves can be used to treat persistent air leaks in children

quiz.question: What is the purpose of endobronchial valves in children?
quiz.answer: To treat persistent air leaks or bronchopleural fistulas

ai.headline: Mpox knowledge gaps found in Burundi
ai.summary: A nationwide survey in Burundi studied people's knowledge and perceptions of mpox. Most participants had heard of mpox, but gaps in knowledge remain, especially among lower-income groups. The survey found that higher income was associated with better mpox knowledge.

items.title: What is the effectiveness of stress interventions for men: a systematic review

ai.headline: Stress interventions for men lack evidence
ai.summary: A systematic review examined the effectiveness of stress interventions for men, including medication, meditation, and therapy. The review found 16 studies, but most had methodological limitations. The findings suggest a lack of evidence on the effectiveness of stress interventions for men.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because men are more likely to experience maladaptive coping behaviours and take their own lives, making effective stress interventions crucial.

items.title: Income Volatility and Parenting Styles during Hard Times

ai.headline: Income ups and downs are linked to changes in how some parents interact with their children.
ai.summary: Researchers used UK household data to see whether changing incomes affect parenting styles. They found that income instability is linked to lower warmth and higher harshness or permissiveness, especially among higher-income parents, while lower-income parents showed different patterns with benefit income gains.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that financial ups and downs, not just average income, may shape everyday family interactions and parenting.
ai.fact: Parenting styles are linked to income volatility, and the patterns differ by parent gender and whether the family started above or below the median income.

quiz.question: Which parents had lower warmth scores when their labour income became unstable?
quiz.answer: Higher-income mothers and higher-income fathers had lower warmth scores linked to labour income instability or earnings losses.

ai.caveat: It is a single preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and it relies on observational data rather than a randomised trial.

items.title: BurnCare: A deep learning framework for burn injury assessment and TBSA estimation.

ai.headline: AI helps assess burn injuries
ai.summary: Researchers developed BurnCare, a deep learning framework to assess burn injuries and estimate total burn surface area. The platform uses a smartphone photograph to estimate the area. It was compared to estimates from healthcare professionals and showed strong performance.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because accurate burn injury assessment is crucial for proper treatment and referral decisions, especially in resource-limited settings.
ai.life_skill: Try to learn about new technologies that can aid in medical assessments.
ai.fact: Burn injuries affect over seven million people annually in India, with limited dedicated burn centres.

quiz.question: How does BurnCare estimate burn injuries?
quiz.answer: BurnCare estimates burn injuries from a single smartphone photograph.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint study, not yet peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Optimizing a Technology-based Body and Mind Intervention

ai.headline: A trial is testing whether an in-home exercise program helps older adults match their fear of falling to their actual fall risk.
ai.summary: This registered trial tests the Physio-fEedback Exercise pRogram (PEER) against an attention control in older adults. It will measure balance, fall risk, physical activity, exercise adherence, and changes in fall-risk appraisal and attitudes to ageing over nine months, including three- and six-month follow-ups.
ai.why_it_matters: It addresses how older adults can stay safe and active by aligning their perceived fall risk with their physical risk.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your worry about falling matches your actual steadiness, and discuss any mismatch with a health professional.
ai.fact: Older adults can either overestimate or underestimate their physical risk of falling.

quiz.question: What is the PEER program designed to help older adults do?
quiz.answer: Improve balance, align perceived fall risk with physical fall risk, and prevent falls.

ai.caveat: This is a trial record with posted results, not a peer-reviewed publication, so the findings have not yet been independently verified.

items.title: Academic motivation and basic psychological needs among university students in physical education and mountain sports: a self-determination theory study

ai.headline: Students' sense of choice and support at university links to their motivation quality.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 237 first- and second-year physical education and mountain sports students about their psychological needs and motivation. They found that greater need satisfaction was linked to stronger autonomous motivation, while greater need frustration was linked to stronger amotivation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how supported and self-directed students feel may shape whether they study willingly or disengage.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your studies feel self-chosen and supported, or pressured and blocked.
ai.fact: Higher need satisfaction was linked to higher autonomous motivation, and higher need frustration was linked to higher amotivation in this student group.

quiz.question: What was most often named as a source of demotivation?
quiz.answer: Curriculum, teaching, and assessment were the most frequently reported demotivation factors.

ai.caveat: Because the data were collected at one point in time at a single university, the results cannot prove cause and effect or generalise to all students.

items.title: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents

ai.headline: A coding library can stop AI agents from making unauthorised changes without hurting their success rate.
ai.summary: Researchers tested Concordat, a Python library that enforces rules on AI agents at runtime, against a standard agent on 50 airline booking tasks. The standard agent made changes without required customer confirmation in 13 of 50 tasks with one model and 29 of 128 runs with another, while Concordat made none and succeeded just as often.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that technical safeguards, not just polite prompts, are needed before AI agents handle real-world tasks like refunds or cancellations.
ai.life_skill: Ask whether any AI assistant you use is technically blocked from making changes without your explicit confirmation.
ai.fact: Software protocols can prevent LLM agents from skipping safety steps such as user confirmation without reducing task success.

quiz.question: What happened when researchers pressured agents to skip customer confirmation on airline tasks?
quiz.answer: The standard agent made unauthorised changes in many runs, while the Concordat agent made none.

ai.caveat: This is a single, not-yet-peer-reviewed preprint tested only on 50 airline tasks with two models, so the results may not generalise.

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations

ai.headline: A new open AI model understands text, images, audio and video together while using less computing power.
ai.summary: Researchers built EmbeddingGemma 2, an open model that represents text, images, audio, video and mixtures in one shared space. It outperformed specialist models and much larger models across embedding benchmarks, while offering options to run on limited hardware.
ai.why_it_matters: It points toward future apps that can search and organise text, images, audio and video together on ordinary devices.
ai.fact: EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model that natively handles text, images, audio, video and combinations in a unified space.

quiz.question: What types of media does EmbeddingGemma 2 represent in a single shared space?
quiz.answer: It natively represents text, images, audio, video and combinations thereof in a unified space.

ai.caveat: The findings come from a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed and are based on the authors' own benchmarks.

items.title: As ancient oceans warmed, carbon export and fish productivity surged

ai.headline: Ancient ocean warming was linked to more carbon export and higher fish productivity
ai.summary: The study looked at how ancient oceans responded as they warmed. It found that carbon export and fish productivity both surged during those warming periods.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps us understand how ocean life and carbon cycles might respond as the climate warms today.

items.title: Exploring the antimicrobial potential of streptococcal fratricins

ai.headline: Lab-tested bacterial enzymes can kill several streptococci, including tooth-decay species.
ai.summary: Researchers screened nine potential fratricins and purified three: Zoocin A, ScrM, and CbpD-ves. All three mainly targeted streptococci, with Zoocin A active against species linked to dental caries and severe human infections, and both Zoocin A and ScrM remained active under body-like conditions.

ai.fact: Zoocin A and ScrM kept working under physiologically relevant pH, temperature, and ionic strength.

ai.headline: Scientists found ways to target aging “zombie cells,” including a tomato compound, in mice.
ai.summary: Seven studies looked at aging cells that cause inflammation and disease. Researchers identified new ways to target them, including a natural compound found in tomatoes. In aging mice, treatments reduced inflammation and improved physical and brain health.
ai.why_it_matters: It points toward future therapies that might slow some biological processes behind aging.
ai.fact: Aging cells that linger in the body are linked to inflammation and disease.

quiz.answer: They reduced inflammation and improved physical and brain health.

ai.headline: Colorectal cancer biology changes with patient age, according to a new tumour cell atlas.
ai.summary: Researchers created a detailed map of cells from 189 colorectal tumours taken from patients aged 20 to over 90. The map reveals features of the cancer that are linked to the patient’s age.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps scientists understand why bowel cancer may differ in younger and older people, which could shape future research and care.

items.title: Should doctors be on social media?

ai.headline: Many people in the UK use social media and AI chatbots for health guidance, and some doctors share medical knowledge online.
ai.summary: The piece describes a geriatrician who began using Instagram at 45 and now shares short medical videos with 290,000 followers. A UK survey of 2,000 people found nearly one in four turn to social media and AI chatbots for health guidance.

items.title: Loose coupling between Ca 2+ channels and release sensors as a synaptic correlate of higher-order brain function

ai.headline: Brain cell connections in mice are wired differently in thinking areas versus sensory areas.
ai.summary: Researchers compared synapses in the prefrontal cortex and primary somatosensory cortex of mice. They found that synapses in the thinking area used loose microdomain coupling, while those in the sensory area used tight nanodomain coupling, affecting timing, strength, and adaptability.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how the same types of brain cells can support different functions like sensation and complex thought.
ai.fact: The physical arrangement of calcium channels and release sensors at synapses differs between brain areas in mice.

quiz.question: Which brain area showed loose microdomain coupling in the mouse synapses studied?
quiz.answer: The prefrontal cortex showed loose microdomain coupling, unlike the primary somatosensory cortex.

ai.caveat: This is a single study in mice, so the findings may not apply to humans.

items.title: Insuring Landlords -- by Thomas Bézy, Antoine B. Levy, Timothy McQuade

ai.headline: A French rent guarantee helped fragile tenants rent homes and move to higher-wage areas.
ai.summary: The study looked at Visale, a free public rent guarantee in France that insures landlords against unpaid rent. It found the scheme improved access to private rental housing for immigrants, newly formed households and low-income renters, and helped people move long distances to expensive, high-wage neighbourhoods at a moderate cost per move.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how insuring landlords can open up housing and job opportunities for people who might otherwise be turned away.
ai.life_skill: Check whether a rent guarantee or deposit scheme is available in your area before applying to rent a home.
ai.fact: Visale is a publicly funded rent guarantee insurance policy in France that is free for eligible tenants and landlords.

quiz.question: What did the French rent guarantee Visale do for eligible tenants?
quiz.answer: It increased their access to private-sector rental housing and helped them move to expensive, high-wage neighbourhoods.
